w: Napier Prison opened in 1862 and held inmates until 1993, making it New Zealand's oldest surviving prison complex. After 131 years as a working jail, the cellblocks reopened to the public as a visitor attraction, swapping bars and lockdowns for tours through the same landings and cells.
s: New Zealand's oldest prison, now open for tours
_facts: Built in 1862 in Napier, New Zealand
Decommissioned as a working prison in 1993
Now operates as a visitor attraction

w: Napier's aquarium started in 1957 and moved to its present Marine Parade site in 1976, where Napier City Council still runs it today. Alongside the fish tanks, exhibits hold kiwi, tuatara, turtles, little penguins and lizards, folding a slice of native New Zealand wildlife into a marine display.
s: Marine Parade aquarium with kiwi and tuatara too
_facts: Public aquarium on Marine Parade, Napier, formerly Napier Aquarium
Started in 1957, moved to its present location in 1976
Exhibits include fish, kiwi, tuatara, turtles, little penguins and lizards

w: Unveiled on Marine Parade in 1954, the bronze Statue of Pania honours a figure of Maori mythology, modelled on Hukarere Girls College student Mei Irihapiti Robin and cast in Carrara, Italy. Often compared to Copenhagen's Little Mermaid, it survived a 1982 shooting and a 2005 theft before recovery.
s: Bronze Maori legend on Marine Parade, twice attacked
_facts: Also known as Pania of the Reef, commissioned by the Thirty Thousand Club
Modelled on Hukarere Girls College student Mei Irihapiti Robin; clay model made by a Carrara, Italy marble company
Unveiled 10 June 1954 by Prime Minister Sidney Holland
Shot in the head in 1982 and stolen in October 2005; recovered and restored within weeks
